nodes.name: Mo-PDA Precipitation
nodes.procedure: 120 mg of (NH4)6Mo7O24·4H2O and 120 mg of dopamine hydrochloride were dissolved in 32 mL of DIW and 64 mL of absolute ethyl alcohol, respectively, under vigorous stirring for half an hour to form uniform colorless transparent liquids (solution A and B). Solution B was slowly poured into solution A (color becomes orange turbid). Then 0.6 mL of NH3·H2O (28 wt.%) was injected and stirred for 6 h. The orange precipitate (Mo-PDA) was washed and centrifuged three times with alcohol and dried at 60°C overnight.

nodes.name: Mo2C/C Calcination
nodes.procedure: Finally, a certain quality of powder was put into a tube furnace and annealed at 800°C for 3 h under 5% H2/Ar with a slow temperature ramping rate of 3°C min^-1.
nodes.source_text: Finally, a certain quality of powder was put into a tube furnace and annealed at 800°C for 3 h under 5% H2/Ar...

nodes.name: Ru Impregnation on Mo2C/C
nodes.procedure: 30 mg of Mo2C/C was dispersed in 20 mL DIW by magnetic stirring for 30 min. Then 0.7 mL RuCl3·xH2O (10 mg/mL) was slowly added and stirred for 4 h at ambient conditions. The precursor was collected by centrifugation, washed 3x with absolute ethanol, and dried at 60°C for 12 h.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of Mo2C-Ru/C: 30 mg of Mo2C/C was added into 20 mL of DIW... dried at 60°C for 12 h.

nodes.name: Mo2C-Ru/C Final Annealing
nodes.procedure: The catalysts were achieved via annealing treatment at 300°C for 2 h under N2 atmosphere.
nodes.source_text: The catalysts were achieved via annealing treatment at 300°C for 2 h under N2 atmosphere.

nodes.description: HER performance on carbon paper in 1 M KOH (industrial current density)
nodes.source_text: the Mo₂C-Ru/C ink is drip-coated on carbon paper (CP) (mass loading: 1mgcm⁻²) and directly tested in 1M KOH electrolyte. At a low overpotential of 180mV, the Mo₂C-Ru/C-CP electrode can achieve the industrial current density of 500mA cm⁻² with robust stability up to 200h

nodes.characterization_summary: The crystallinity of Mo₂C in Mo₂C-Ru/C is reduced and can be assigned to α-Mo₂C; characteristic peaks of Ru are not observed due to low content or small size.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystallinity of Mo₂C in Mo₂C-Ru/C is reduced (Figure S7a, Supporting Information), possibly being destroyed by the RuCl₃ aqueous solution with acidic nature and the Mo₂C in Mo₂C-Ru/C can be assigned to α-Mo₂C.

nodes.evidence_snippet: The HAADF-STEM image and corresponding elemental mapping images indicate that Ru, Mo, and C elements are homogeneously distributed in Mo₂C-Ru/C (Figure 2f).
The mass loading of Ru is ≈2.1 wt.% ... as confirmed by inductively coupled plasma-atomic emission spectroscopy ... (Figure S7c and Table S1, Supporting Information).
the content of carbon in Mo₂C-Ru/C is ≈59.6% as confirmed by ... thermogravimetric analysis (Figure S7c and Table S1, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey confirms presence of Mo, Ru, C, N; Mo 3d shows Mo²⁺ (Mo₂C), Mo⁴⁺, Mo⁶⁺ (surface oxidation) shifted to lower binding energy vs Mo₂C/C; Ru 3p peaks at 484.1 and 462.0 eV confirm metallic Ru⁰, shifted to higher energy vs Ru/C indicating electron transfer from Ru to Mo₂C; C 1s shows C-C/C=C (284.79 eV), C-N (285.59 eV), O-C=O (288.02 eV), Mo-C (284.4 eV); N 1s shows graphitic N (397.93 eV), pyrrolic N (395.50 eV), pyridinic N (394.70 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The presence of Mo, Ru, C, and N elements in Mo₂C-Ru/C is disclosed by the survey spectrum (Figure 3a). ... the high-resolution Mo 3d spectra of both Mo₂C-Ru/C and Mo₂C/C can be deconvoluted into three double peaks ... The peaks with binding energies of 484.1 and 462.0 eV in the Ru 3p spectra can be attributed to the 3p₁/₂ and 3p₃/₂ of metallic Ru⁰ ... Compared with Ru/C, the Ru 3p XPS spectrum of Mo₂C-Ru/C shifts to higher energy, indicating electron transfer from Ru to Mo₂C. The high-resolution C 1s can be divided into four pronounced peaks of C-C/C=C (284.79 eV), C-N (285.59 eV), O-C=O (288.02 eV), and Mo-C (284.4 eV). The peaks located at 397.93, 395.50, and 394.70 eV in the N 1s spectra can be assigned to graphitic N, pyrrolic N, and pyridinic N.
